title: Sales Discovery Call — Acme Corp
description: Discovery call with Acme's ops team about meeting automation.
transcript: 00:05 Sarah Watts: Hi Tom, hi Emily — thanks for making time today. I believe we're exploring how Fireflies could fit into your team's workflow, so let's start with what's on your mind.
00:21 Tom Reyes: Thanks Sarah. Basically, our sales team runs around 40 discovery and demo calls a week, and we lose so much time writing notes and updating the CRM afterwards.
00:36 Sarah Watts: Got it — how are you capturing those calls today?

00:41 Tom Reyes: Honestly, it's a mess. Some people type notes live, others write them after the call, and about half the details never make it into HubSpot. Our reps spend maybe 3 hours a day on notes and admin.
00:59 Emily Chen: And from a management perspective, I can't answer simple questions like which objections came up this week without asking every rep individually.

01:12 Sarah Watts: That's exactly the pattern we see with teams your size. Fireflies joins your calls automatically, transcribes everything, and generates a structured summary — overview, action items, topics, and metrics — within minutes of the call ending.
01:30 Tom Reyes: Does it work with Google Meet? That's our main platform.
01:35 Sarah Watts: Yes — Google Meet, Zoom, and Teams, plus uploaded audio and video files if you have existing recordings.
01:44 Tom Reyes: What about accuracy? We had a bad experience with another notetaker last year — the transcripts were unusable.

01:53 Sarah Watts: I hear you. Our transcription is best-in-class, around 95% accurate, and it handles overlapping speech and noisy environments. I'm happy to run a live demo on a real call so you can judge for yourself.
02:10 Emily Chen: That would help. Can you also show how the CRM sync works? If this doesn't reduce our HubSpot admin time, it's a non-starter.
02:21 Sarah Watts: Absolutely. Notes and action items push to HubSpot automatically, and we can tag calls by deal stage. Let me show you a sample call summary in the Notepad view.
02:34 Tom Reyes: This is the transcript view? Clicking a line jumps the audio?
02:40 Sarah Watts: Exactly — every timestamp is clickable, and you can search within the transcript or filter by questions, tasks, metrics, or pricing mentions.
02:51 Emily Chen: The pricing filter would be great for deal reviews. How much is this, by the way?
02:58 Sarah Watts: The Growth plan is $19 per user per month, billed annually, and the Pro plan is $29 per user per month with unlimited recordings and advanced analytics.
03:12 Tom Reyes: What's the difference for us at 120 seats?

03:16 Sarah Watts: At 120 seats, Growth runs about $2,280 a month. Pro would be $3,480. Given your volume — 40 calls a week — I'd actually start a pilot on Pro for the sales team only, maybe 25 seats, and evaluate for 30 days.
03:36 Tom Reyes: That's an interesting approach. Our budget is capped at $30k this quarter for new tools, so a pilot in that range would fit.
03:47 Emily Chen: I'd want the security review done before we roll anything out. What's your posture there?

03:54 Sarah Watts: We're SOC 2 Type 2 certified, GDPR and HIPAA compliant, with 256-bit encryption in transit and at rest. I'll send our security documentation and the standard questionnaire after this call.
04:08 Tom Reyes: Great, that goes to our legal team. What does onboarding look like? We're not super technical.
04:16 Sarah Watts: It's genuinely light — you connect your calendar, set which meetings the notetaker should join, and you're live. Most teams are fully onboarded in under an hour.
04:29 Emily Chen: Can we control which meetings it joins? Some of our calls are sensitive.
04:35 Sarah Watts: Yes, you can set it to join only external calls, only meetings with a web-conferencing link, or fully manual. Admins can also set team-wide policies.
04:48 Tom Reyes: What kind of ROI are your similar teams seeing?
04:53 Sarah Watts: Teams like yours typically report about 5 hours saved per rep per week and a 30% lift in CRM data completeness. For 25 reps, that's meaningful.
05:07 Emily Chen: The ROI math works if the pilot proves the accuracy claim. Tom, shall we propose the pilot to leadership next week?
05:16 Tom Reyes: Yes. Sarah, can you send the pilot proposal with the 25-seat pricing? I'd like it before our leadership sync on Thursday.
05:26 Sarah Watts: Will do — proposal with the 25-seat breakdown and the security docs, both by tomorrow.
05:33 Tom Reyes: Perfect. And can we schedule a technical deep-dive? Our IT lead, Priya at our end, will want to poke at the integrations.
05:42 Sarah Watts: Of course. I'll send a scheduling link for next week — does Tuesday or Wednesday work better?
05:48 Tom Reyes: Wednesday afternoon is better for us.
05:52 Sarah Watts: Wednesday it is. I'll also include a demo recording you can share with the wider team.
05:59 Emily Chen: One last question — what happens to our data if we leave?
06:05 Sarah Watts: You own your data. Everything is exportable — transcripts, summaries, and recordings — and we offer zero data retention options if that's a compliance requirement.
06:17 Emily Chen: That's reassuring. Okay, I think we have what we need.
06:22 Tom Reyes: Thanks Sarah, this was genuinely one of the more useful vendor calls we've had.
06:27 Sarah Watts: Thank you both. I'll follow up tomorrow — talk Wednesday!

summary.overview: Discovery call with Acme Corp (120-seat ops team, ~40 sales calls/week). Tom and Emily's core pain: reps lose ~3 hours daily to notes and CRM admin, and management lacks visibility into objections. Fireflies was positioned around the Notepad demo, HubSpot sync, and a recommended 25-seat Pro pilot. Budget cap is $30k this quarter; a security review and leadership sync on Thursday gate the proposal. Next steps: send pilot pricing + security docs by tomorrow, technical deep-dive Wednesday.
